prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a low-speed head-on collision in Houston, Texas, and has neck and back strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1317; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for agreeing to give a recorded statement today. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd prefer to leave my name off the recording, if that's okay. You already have it on the claim.
Q: That's fine. Can you describe where you were driving when the collision happened?
A: I was on a main road in Houston, heading toward a shopping center. It was a weekday afternoon and traffic was moving slowly.
Q: What happened right before the impact?
A: The car in front of me stopped suddenly. I braked, but the vehicle behind me had already been closing in, and it didn't stop in time. I think it was going maybe ten or fifteen miles an hour when it hit me.
Q: Which part of your vehicle was struck?
A: The rear bumper of the car I was driving took most of it. Actually, I should say it was a head-on, so I mean the front of my car. I got those mixed up because I was turning around in my seat at the time.
Q: Understood. Were you wearing your seatbelt?
A: Yes, I was.
Q: Did the airbags deploy?
A: No, they didn't. The impact was not strong enough for that.
Q: How are you feeling since the collision?
A: My neck is stiff and sore, especially when I turn my head to the left. My lower back aches, and sitting for long periods makes it worse. I've been taking over-the-counter pain relievers and using a heating pad.
Q: Have you seen a medical provider?
A: Yes, I went to an urgent care clinic the same day. They examined me and told me it looked like a neck and back strain, and they gave me a follow-up plan.
Q: Is there anything else you would like to add?
A: Only that I want to get back to normal as soon as possible. Thank you for your time.
